story_description: Implement the foundational Swift components for the Advanced Hooks Builder including type definitions, validation, input/output schemas, pattern matching, environment variable reference, testing infrastructure, and JSON export capabilities.
task_description: Create HookTestRunner actor that enables users to test command hooks with sample input data before deployment, executing scripts in a controlled environment and providing structured test results with parsed output, exit codes, duration metrics, and error diagnostics.
atom_description: Implement HookTestRunner actor with testCommandHook method that spawns hook scripts with JSON-encoded HookInput via stdin, captures stdout/stderr, handles timeouts, parses output as HookOutput, and returns TestResult struct containing success status, raw output, exit code, execution duration, parsed output, and error collection. Also implement generateTestCommand helper for CLI debugging.
problem_statement: Hook developers need a way to test their hooks before deploying them to production. Currently, testing requires manually crafting JSON input, running scripts in terminal, and parsing output by hand. This is error-prone and slow. A built-in test runner that accepts structured input, executes hooks in isolation, captures all output streams, parses results as HookOutput, and provides clear pass/fail feedback will dramatically improve the hook development experience and reduce broken hook deployments.

assumptions: HookInput and HookOutput types are defined in HookTypes.swift and are Codable
Hooks are bash scripts that read JSON from stdin and write JSON to stdout
The /bin/bash shell is available on all macOS systems (macOS standard)
Temporary directory from FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory is writable
POSIX permission 0o755 is sufficient for script execution
Script execution completes or times out within 60 seconds by default
Hook scripts follow Claude Code hook protocol (JSON in, JSON out)
UTF-8 encoding is used for all JSON serialization and script content
constraints: Must use actor isolation to prevent data races during concurrent test runs
Must not leave temporary files on disk after test completion (use defer for cleanup)
Must handle script paths with spaces and special characters via proper quoting
Must escape single quotes in JSON input when constructing echo command
Must terminate runaway processes when timeout is exceeded
Must capture both stdout and stderr separately for diagnostic purposes
Must work with both inline script content and external script paths
Must not block main thread during script execution (use async/await properly)
functional_requirements: FR1: HookTestRunner shall be declared as a public actor to ensure thread-safe test execution
FR2: TestResult shall be a Sendable struct containing success (Bool), output (String), exitCode (Int), duration (TimeInterval), parsedOutput (HookOutput?), and errors ([String])
FR3: testCommandHook shall accept command (String), input (HookInput), and optional timeout (TimeInterval defaulting to 60) parameters
FR4: testCommandHook shall detect inline scripts (not starting with / or $) and write them to temporary files with 0o755 permissions
FR5: testCommandHook shall substitute $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR with FileManager.default.currentDirectoryPath in script paths
FR6: testCommandHook shall substitute $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with currentDirectoryPath + /.claude in script paths
FR7: testCommandHook shall encode HookInput as JSON using JSONEncoder for stdin pipe
FR8: testCommandHook shall spawn /bin/bash -c with echo piping JSON to script via stdin
FR9: testCommandHook shall escape single quotes in JSON input using '\'' replacement pattern
FR10: testCommandHook shall capture stdout and stderr via separate Pipe instances
FR11: testCommandHook shall implement timeout using DispatchSemaphore with .wait(timeout:) returning .timedOut on expiration
FR12: testCommandHook shall terminate process and return failure TestResult when timeout is exceeded
FR13: testCommandHook shall parse stdout as HookOutput using JSONDecoder when output is non-empty
FR14: testCommandHook shall append parse errors to errors array when JSON decoding fails
FR15: testCommandHook shall append stderr content to errors array when stderr is non-empty
FR16: testCommandHook shall calculate success as exitCode == 0 AND errors.isEmpty
FR17: testCommandHook shall calculate duration using Date().timeIntervalSince(startTime)
FR18: testCommandHook shall clean up temporary script files in defer block using FileManager.removeItem
FR19: generateTestCommand shall accept scriptPath (String) and input (HookInput) parameters
FR20: generateTestCommand shall return shell command string with properly escaped JSON and script path
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Test execution overhead (excluding script runtime) shall be under 50ms
NFR2: Memory usage during test shall not exceed 10MB excluding script output buffers
NFR3: Timeout precision shall be within 100ms of specified timeout value
NFR4: Actor isolation shall prevent data races when running concurrent tests
NFR5: Temporary file cleanup shall occur in all code paths including error and timeout cases
NFR6: JSON encoding/decoding shall handle all HookInput and HookOutput field types without data loss
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file HookTestRunner.swift in Blaze/Sources/Settings/Hooks/ directory
Step 2: Add Foundation import at top of file
Step 3: Define public actor HookTestRunner with no stored properties (stateless service)
Step 4: Define TestResult struct inside actor with public access and Sendable conformance
Step 5: Add TestResult properties: success (Bool), output (String), exitCode (Int), duration (TimeInterval), parsedOutput (HookOutput?), errors ([String])
Step 6: Implement testCommandHook method signature with command, input, timeout parameters
Step 7: Record startTime using Date() at method entry
Step 8: Implement script path resolution: check if command starts with / or $ to determine inline vs external
Step 9: For inline scripts: create temp file path using temporaryDirectory + UUID, write command, set permissions 0o755
Step 10: For external scripts: replace $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with resolved paths
Step 11: Add defer block to delete temp file if cleanup flag is true
Step 12: Encode HookInput to JSON using JSONEncoder, convert to String with UTF-8
Step 13: Create Process instance with executableURL = /bin/bash
Step 14: Set process arguments to [-c, echo 'JSON' | scriptPath] with escaped single quotes
Step 15: Create outputPipe and errorPipe as Pipe instances, assign to standardOutput and standardError
Step 16: Call process.run() wrapped in try to handle launch failures
Step 17: Create DispatchSemaphore with value 0 for timeout coordination
Step 18: Dispatch async block that calls process.waitUntilExit() then signals semaphore
Step 19: Wait on semaphore with timeout, check for .timedOut result
Step 20: On timeout: call process.terminate(), return failure TestResult with timeout error message
Step 21: Read outputData and errorData from pipes using readDataToEndOfFile()
Step 22: Convert outputData to String with UTF-8 encoding, default to empty string
Step 23: Convert errorData to String with UTF-8 encoding, default to empty string
Step 24: Get exitCode from process.terminationStatus as Int
Step 25: Calculate duration using Date().timeIntervalSince(startTime)
Step 26: Initialize empty errors array and nil parsedOutput
Step 27: If output is non-empty after trimming, attempt JSONDecoder.decode as HookOutput
Step 28: On decode failure, append parse error message to errors array with localizedDescription
Step 29: If errorOutput is non-empty, append stderr: prefix + content to errors array
Step 30: Construct and return TestResult with all collected values
Step 31: Implement generateTestCommand method with scriptPath and input parameters
Step 32: Encode input using JSONEncoder with sortedKeys for deterministic output
Step 33: Construct shell command string with echo, escaped JSON, pipe, and bash scriptPath
Step 34: Return formatted command string suitable for copy-paste to terminal
Step 35: Add documentation comments to all public types and methods
data_model_changes: New actor HookTestRunner: Stateless service actor for executing hook tests in isolation
New struct TestResult: Sendable value type containing success (Bool), output (String), exitCode (Int), duration (TimeInterval), parsedOutput (HookOutput?), errors ([String])
No database changes: Test runner is ephemeral with no persistence requirements
No model migrations: New types only, no modifications to existing types
api_contracts: HookTestRunner.testCommandHook(command: String, input: HookInput, timeout: TimeInterval = 60) async throws -> TestResult - Executes command hook with provided input and returns structured test result
HookTestRunner.generateTestCommand(scriptPath: String, input: HookInput) throws -> String - Returns shell command for manual debugging in terminal
TestResult.success: Bool - True if exitCode is 0 and no errors occurred
TestResult.output: String - Raw stdout content from hook execution
TestResult.exitCode: Int - Process termination status (0 = success)
TestResult.duration: TimeInterval - Execution time in seconds
TestResult.parsedOutput: HookOutput? - Decoded hook output if valid JSON returned
TestResult.errors: [String] - Collection of error messages including stderr and parse failures
event_contracts: No custom events emitted: Test runner is a synchronous service with result returned directly
HookOutput parsed from stdout follows existing HookOutput contract with result field (continue/block/error) and optional message field
Actor isolation ensures no concurrent state mutations requiring event coordination

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Command string is empty - should throw or return error immediately without spawning process
Edge case 2: Script path contains spaces - must be quoted properly in bash -c argument
Edge case 3: HookInput contains single quotes - must escape as '\'' to prevent shell injection
Edge case 4: Hook script does not exist - process will fail with file not found, captured in stderr
Edge case 5: Hook script is not executable - permission denied error captured in stderr
Edge case 6: Hook outputs invalid JSON - parse fails gracefully, raw output still available in result
Edge case 7: Hook outputs valid JSON but wrong schema - decode fails, error message includes decoding details
Edge case 8: Hook outputs nothing (empty stdout) - parsedOutput is nil, not an error condition
Edge case 9: Hook writes to stderr but exits 0 - success is false because errors array is non-empty
Edge case 10: Hook hangs indefinitely - timeout fires, process terminated, timeout error returned
Edge case 11: Hook exits immediately with non-zero code - failure captured with stderr content
Edge case 12: Temporary file creation fails - throw error from write operation, no cleanup needed
Edge case 13: Multiple concurrent tests - actor isolation ensures each test has independent state
Edge case 14: Process spawn fails - try/catch around process.run() handles launch errors
Edge case 15: Very large stdout output (megabytes) - memory handled by Data, may hit practical limits
failure_modes: FM1: Script not found error - Display: Hook script not found at path. Check: script path and $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR resolution
FM2: Permission denied error - Display: Cannot execute hook script. Suggestion: Run chmod +x on the script file
FM3: Timeout exceeded - Display: Hook execution timed out after N seconds. Suggestion: Increase timeout or optimize hook
FM4: JSON parse failure - Display: Hook output is not valid JSON. Show raw output for debugging
FM5: Process spawn failure - Display: Failed to start hook process. Check system resources and bash availability
FM6: Temporary file write failure - Display: Cannot create temporary script file. Check disk space and permissions
FM7: UTF-8 encoding failure - Display: Hook output contains invalid characters. Check script encoding
FM8: Script crashes or segfaults - Display: Hook process terminated abnormally (signal N). Check script for bugs

risks: Risk 1: Shell injection via malicious HookInput JSON values if escaping is incorrect
Risk 2: Resource exhaustion if hook scripts spawn many child processes or consume excessive memory
Risk 3: Zombie processes if timeout termination does not properly clean up process tree
Risk 4: Race condition if semaphore signaling and process exit status reading have timing issues
Risk 5: Temp file collisions if UUID generation has issues (extremely unlikely)
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Use proper single quote escaping with '\'' pattern tested against injection vectors
Mitigation 2: Set process resource limits via Process configuration if issues arise in practice
Mitigation 3: Use process.terminate() which sends SIGTERM; consider SIGKILL fallback if needed
Mitigation 4: Read exit status only after waitUntilExit completes, semaphore coordinates async wait
Mitigation 5: UUID collision is astronomically unlikely; temp directory isolation provides additional safety
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to hook testing feature only. Test runner is isolated service with no impact on actual hook execution in production. Failed tests do not affect session state, settings, or other Blaze functionality. Temp file leak would only affect /tmp disk space.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If test runner proves unreliable, disable Run Test button in UI and direct users to use generateTestCommand for manual terminal testing. The generateTestCommand method is simpler and can serve as fallback. No user data affected as test results are ephemeral.
